hypotheses.justification: If R ≤ 0, then R/2 ≤ 0, so `ball x₀ (R / 2) = ∅` (`Metric.ball_eq_empty`). Then `mu.restrict ∅ = 0` and every `∀ᵐ` statement for that measure holds, including the conclusion. The proof uses hR only to show `ball x₀ (R/2) ⊆ ball x₀ R` (via `half_le_self hR.le`) and so get `hhalf`. So the new proof starts with `rcases le_or_lt R 0`: if R ≤ 0 the conclusion is trivial as above, and if R > 0 the existing proof runs unchanged with the local fact `0 < R`.

`0 ≤ K` follows from the other hypotheses (keeping hR). Suppose K < 0. Take k = 0 and w = `W1p.contDiffComp … invApprox (c 0) … u`, exactly as in the proof. The existing argument (`hw`, which does not use hK) gives `hsub w …`: a.e. on ball x₀ (R/2), `value w x ≤ K * I^{p⁻¹}` with I = ∫ max(...)^p ≥ 0. Since `Real.rpow_nonneg` gives I^{p⁻¹} ≥ 0, the right side is ≤ 0. By `hval` and `hum` (restricted with `hhalf`), a.e. on that ball `value w x = invApprox c (u x) = u x / (u x² + c²) > 0`, because u x ≥ m > 0. These two facts contradict each other a.e., so `mu (ball x₀ (R/2)) = 0`. But R > 0 makes the ball nonempty and open, and an add-Haar measure is `IsOpenPosMeasure`, so the ball has positive measure (`Metric.measure_ball_pos`). Hence K ≥ 0, and the rest of the proof (`mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left … hK`) goes through with this derived fact. hR and hK can also be deleted together: in the case R > 0 this argument applies, and the case R ≤ 0 is trivial.
